newsitem.title: USA: Legend settlement rejected, faces delisting.
newsitem.headline: Legend settlement rejected, faces delisting.

text.p: Legend Properties Inc said a Delaware court rejected a settlement it had reached in a class action suit, which may result in its delisting from Nasdaq.

Legend said its reviewing the opinion and studying options. The suit was brought against Banyan Mortgage Investment Fund which was bought by RGI U.S. Holdings on December 31, 1996 for $22 million, said chief financial officer Ray Whitty. The new firm was named Legend Properties.
The suit claimed Banyan's board did not properly review options before aggreeing to the deal and sought greater value for shareholders, Whitty said.

The court rejected the settlement because it did not believe the named plaintiffs were adequate class representatives, Legend said in a release. Whitty said two out of 22,000 shareholders involved in the suit objected to the settlement which involved restructuring of about $32 million debt owed to the company's majority shareholder, RGI.
Legend's stock has remained on Nasdaq via an exception from certain filing requirements, which expires July 31.
Legend said until certain uncertainties surrounding the class action lawsuit are removed it cannot obtain an opinion from independent auditors, which will result in delisting.
